shows.description: Grammy-winning pianist and producer who bridges jazz, hip-hop, and R&B. Glasper's Black Radio albums redefined modern jazz for a generation — his live shows are loose, funky, and full of surprises.
Alto saxophonist who came up playing with Stevie Wonder and Alicia Keys. Her Phoenix album earned a Grammy nom — fiery, soulful playing rooted in hard bop with a modern edge.
Hammond organ virtuoso who grew up playing in church. Blends gospel, jazz, and funk into euphoric, crowd-moving sets. The Funk Apostles bring a full band energy that's half concert, half revival.

Tenor sax legend with Marilyn Crispell on piano and Carmen Castaldi on drums. Trio Tapestry is intimate, exploratory chamber jazz — spacious and deeply lyrical. A chance to hear a master in a small room.
Oakland-raised trumpeter who's one of the most vital voices in modern jazz. His playing is vulnerable and searching, moving between post-bop intensity and near-silence. Every set feels like an event.
Don Randi is an original Wrecking Crew pianist — he played on everything from Good Vibrations to Strangers in the Night. His weekly residency at the Baked Potato is an LA institution.
Bassist and producer who's played with everyone from Tracy Chapman to Laurie Anderson. His trio leans into progressive jazz-rock — tight, dynamic, and adventurous.
Multi-instrumentalist who plays drums, bass, guitar, and keys simultaneously in a one-person-band setup called fOUR. You have to see it to believe it — truly jaw-dropping musicianship.
Guitarist from Tortoise and one of Chicago's most influential musicians. Parker's solo work blends jazz, electronic, and ambient textures into something hypnotic and uniquely his own.
LA-based pianist with a ferocious post-bop style. Only in her mid-20s, Han channels McCoy Tyner and Herbie Hancock with real authority. One of the most exciting young players on the scene.
Grammy-winning big band that reimagines Thelonious Monk's compositions with a full orchestra. Beasley's arrangements are inventive and swinging — a great introduction to big band jazz.

The tenor saxophonist who brought jazz back to the cultural mainstream. From his work on Kendrick's To Pimp a Butterfly to his epic The Epic, Kamasi packs houses with spiritual, maximalist jazz. Rare club date.
Trumpeter and composer at the heart of LA's young jazz community. McCabe's quintet plays original compositions that move between tight arrangements and open improvisation.
Alto saxophonist and bandleader who's part of LA's new wave of straight-ahead players. Daniels brings a warm, lyrical approach rooted in the jazz tradition with a contemporary voice.
South African-born multi-reed player blending jazz with Cape Town influences. Solomon's group moves between hard-driving post-bop and meditative world music textures.
Bassist and ambient-jazz auteur behind the beloved Wilkes album. His live shows are warm, groovy, and surprisingly danceable — a gateway into LA's modern jazz underground.
Belgian-American duo blending jazz, pop, and art-rock into something completely their own. Zach Phillips and Ma Clément build songs from improvised sessions — catchy, weird, and captivating live.
Drummer, rapper, and producer who makes jazz that sounds like nothing else. Mixes hip-hop production, avant-garde improvisation, and deeply personal lyrics. His Wired albums are essential listening.
Free weekly jazz night at this Eastside bar. Rotating musicians from the local scene in a laid-back, no-cover setting — a great way to discover new players.
Trumpeter and Orenda Records label head who's a cornerstone of LA's creative music scene. Rosenboom's playing spans jazz, prog, and noise — always pushing boundaries. Free show, no excuse to miss it.
Free weekly jazz night at this Eastside bar. Rotating musicians from the local scene in a laid-back, no-cover setting — a great way to discover new players.
Multi-reed experimentalist who processes saxophone through electronics into alien, beautiful soundscapes. Gendel's solo sets are meditative and unpredictable — a unique experience in a sacred space.

Alto saxophonist and composer bridging spectral composition with Senegalese rap. Sélébéyone is one of the most ambitious projects in modern jazz — cerebral, rhythmic, and unlike anything else you'll hear.

Pianist and MacArthur Fellow whose trio with Linda May Han Oh and Tyshawn Sorey is one of the great working groups in jazz. Rhythmically complex, emotionally direct, and stunning in Disney Hall's acoustics.
Weekly open jam session hosted by drummer Kevin Kanner. Musicians sit in throughout the night — you never know who'll show up. A longstanding tradition at one of LA's oldest live music venues.

Slauson Malone 1 is the project of Jasper Marsalis (son of Wynton), making deconstructed art-music that pulls from jazz, noise, and hip-hop. Paired with trumpeter Nicole McCabe for an experimental double bill.
